Subject: Request: temporary SLA exception for burst throttling during month-end analytics

Hi Jordan,

We're ramping a new monthly analytics pipeline that runs a 4-hour intensive scoring job on the 28th of every month. Over the last two runs we've hit Redwood's burst throttle and end up with consistent tail latency spikes that break internal SLAs to our customers. I attached the last run's token/time breakdown (bluepeak_monthly_burst_report.csv).

Can BluePeak apply for a temporary SLA exception that:
- Increases our burst quota by +3x for a 6-hour window on the 28th;
- Guarantees p95 token latency <= 250ms for that window;
- Includes an operational contact and an escalation path if throttling occurs.

We're prepared to pay a premium for reserved burst capacity for the next 3 months while we smooth the workload. Need to know next steps and an estimated lead time.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Park
Head of Platform Engineering
BluePeak Analytics

Hi team — quick technical read after reviewing the CSV. Key notes: 
- The job observes a steep token arrival spike for ~3 hours with many parallel small requests (high request-per-second rather than one large stream). That pattern triggers fairness throttles in the hosted tier.
- Options:
  a) Short-term: provision a temporary Dedicated burst pool (GPUs pinned, isolated queues) for the 6-hour window. This gives us deterministic latency and avoids fairness throttles.
  b) Medium-term: adjust request batching and enable prefix caching for repeated prompts to reduce overall token compute.
  c) Interim: raise per-minute rate limits and set a soft-floor throttling policy (grace queue) for BluePeak.

Operational caveats: dedicated pools require 48–72 hours lead time to guarantee hardware. Soft-floor adjustments can be made in <24 hours but do not fully avoid fairness arbitration under extreme contention. For p95 <= 250ms we should provision Dedicated for the critical window.

Proposed plan for the 28th:
- Canary test on 21st with a 2-hour synthetic replay (we need BluePeak to consent to a shifted window).
- If canary meets p95 target, schedule Dedicated burst for 28th (6 hours).
- Provide an on-call SE (myself) for the window and a direct Slack escalation channel.

I'll attach a short runbook after alignment.

— Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Daniel — commercial framing here. Thank you for flagging this early. High level offer: 

1) Temporary Dedicated Burst: 6-hour reserved window on the 28th for 3 months, priced at a 45% uplift to standard hosted token rates (covers capacity reservation).
2) Latency SLA for the reserved window: p95 token latency <= 250ms. If we miss the p95 target due to Redwood-side failure (excludes customer misconfiguration or network), BluePeak will receive a credit equal to 5% of that month's Reserved Burst fee per incident, up to 30%.
3) Operational add-ons: 24/7 on-call contact during the window, a pre-run canary at a mutually agreed time (we propose the 21st), and a shared runbook.

Could you confirm acceptance of the pricing model and whether BluePeak wants us to draft an amendment now or proceed to a fast-track exception form? If you accept, Legal (Neha) will prepare a short addendum; we can route via DocuSign.

Thanks — Marissa
